newsitem.title: USA: Former Missouri lawmaker acquitted on some counts.
newsitem.headline: Former Missouri lawmaker acquitted on some counts.

text.p: Former Missouri House Speaker Bob Griffin was acquitted Monday on federal charges of bribery, but a jury deadlocked on six other counts.
Griffin was indicted in 1996 with other Missouri power brokers in one of the most far-reaching public corruption investigations in state history.
U.S. Attorney Stephen Hill said he will seek to retry Griffin on the six remaining charges which include racketeering and mail fraud.
While the jury partly acquitted Griffin, it found two of his three co-defendants guilty on other charges.

Mike Fisher, a local labor leader, was found guilty of racketeering and three other charges. Cathryn Simmons, a veteran political consultant, was found guilty on 18 of 20 counts in the public corruption case.
Lobbyist Steven Hurst was acquitted of all charges brought against him.
The four defendants were charged with taking part in a scheme in which Griffin and Fisher allegedly used their influence to help Simmons get $456,000 worth of consulting contracts.
Jurors deliberated for five days last week before announcing Friday they had reached verdicts on only some of the 37 charges against Griffin and his co-defendants.
U.S. District Judge Dean Whipple told jury members to take the weekend off and come back Monday to continue working.
